text:
Calgary lost Kevin Bahl for the season, and that is the story around the Flames right now. Bahl and Simon Nemec were the team's most-used pair, more than 200 minutes together at five on five, and the headlines since have been about who replaces him, from the AHL depth chart to trade targets.

The rest of the picture is a team scrapping for results without much margin. The Flames are 8-10-1, with 45.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and a power play producing just 0.39 expected goals a game. They also take more penalties than they draw. Their shooters have scored about 4.8 fewer goals than their chances deserved, which looks to us like part bad luck and part a lineup short on finishers.

Devin Cooley has been the counterweight. Over his last five starts he is 4-1-0 with a .941 save percentage and 5.1 goals saved above expected, and he was solid again in a 3-1 loss to the Rangers on Wednesday. If there is a reason for optimism, it's that the goaltending has given the skaters a chance most nights.

Our numbers give Calgary a 9% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 78 points. What to watch: how the minutes Bahl leaves behind get shared, and whether a trade fills them.
